swapped.why: Once the banned facts (purple cloth, Thyatira, Macedonian city, opened heart) are removed, the BSB gives too few further distinct facts about the woman Lydia for two new clues, and the Jeremiah and Ezekiel verses describe the land of Lydia rather than her.

After felling Goliath with a stone, David pulled the giant's own from its sheath and cut off his head.
While rebuilding the wall of Jerusalem after the exile, each builder worked with one strapped at his side.
Paul told believers to take the helmet of salvation and the one of the Spirit, which is the word of God.
Ehud made a double-edged one a cubit long and strapped it to his right thigh under his cloak.
When two women each claimed the same baby, King Solomon told his servants to bring him one.
In Ezekiel's vision, one of these reached out and put fire into the hands of the man clothed in linen.
Two of these, made of hammered gold, faced each other at the ends of the mercy seat on the ark.
Figures of these were skillfully worked into the tabernacle veil of blue, purple and scarlet yarn.

Solomon made two of these from olive wood, each ten cubits high, for the temple's inner sanctuary.
In Ezekiel's vision, each of these had four faces, including a man, a lion and an eagle.

In Eden, he gave names to all the livestock, the birds of the air, and every beast of the field.
After the fall in the garden, the LORD God made garments of skin for him and his wife.
After he ate from the forbidden tree, God told him the ground was cursed and he would toil.
In the earliest record of generations, he lived a total of 930 years and then died.
God drove him out of Eden and placed cherubim with a flaming sword to guard the tree of life.
Writing to Corinth, Paul says that as in him all die, so in Christ all will be made alive.
Luke traces the family line of Jesus back through Seth to him, the son of God.
Eve's younger son, he was a keeper of sheep while his older brother worked the soil.
He brought the LORD the best portions of the firstborn of his flock, and God looked on him with favor.
When the LORD asked his brother where he was, the brother answered, "I do not know!"
A New Testament roll of the faithful says he was commended as righteous and by faith still speaks though dead.
The sprinkled blood of Jesus, mediator of a new covenant, speaks a better word than his blood.
Soon after Eden, God said the voice of this son's blood was crying out to Him from the ground.
Jesus warned the scribes and Pharisees about the righteous blood shed on earth, from his blood to Zechariah's.
In the wilderness, Dathan and Abiram of Reuben joined his followers in rebelling against Moses and Aaron.
In the wilderness, the earth opened its mouth and swallowed this rebel's men, their households and all their possessions.
Fire came from the LORD and consumed the 250 men of his group who were offering incense.
Moses told this Levite that the tabernacle work was not enough for him, since he sought the priesthood too.
Eleazar had his followers' bronze censers hammered out to overlay the altar, a reminder that only Aaron's descendants offer incense.
Psalm headings credit his sons with songs, including the one that begins, "As the deer pants for streams of water."
Zelophehad's daughters told Moses their father died in the wilderness but was not among this man's followers.
The first time Noah sent this bird from the ark, it found no place to rest its foot and flew back.
After waiting seven more days, Noah sent this bird out from the ark, and it never returned.
A lover called his beloved this as she stayed in the clefts of the rock, and he asked to hear her sweet voice.
In a psalm, David longed for wings like this bird's so he could fly away and find rest.
The prophet Hosea compared Ephraim to a silly, senseless one of these, calling to Egypt, then Assyria.
Sending the Twelve out like sheep among wolves, Jesus told them to be as innocent as these birds.
Sick and grieving, King Hezekiah said he chirped like a swallow and moaned like this bird.
Serving under Nebuchadnezzar's chief official, he would not defile himself with the king's food or wine.
He went in before Nebuchadnezzar and asked for time so he could give the king the interpretation of his dream.
At King Belshazzar's banquet, he read the writing that said the king was weighed on the scales and found deficient.
After King Darius signed a decree, he still knelt and prayed three times a day by windows open toward Jerusalem.
In the first year of Darius, he learned from Jeremiah's words that Jerusalem's desolation would last seventy years.
Jealous administrators and satraps under King Darius searched for a charge against him but found no corruption or negligence.
Jesus told His followers that this prophet had spoken of the abomination of desolation standing in the holy place.
One night the LORD told Gideon to tear down his father's one for Baal and cut down the Asherah pole beside it.
Abraham arranged wood on this, then bound his son Isaac and laid him on top.
With stones, Elijah built this in the name of the LORD and dug a trench around it.
Afraid of King Solomon, Adonijah ran and took hold of its horns.
In Isaiah's vision, a seraph flew to him with a glowing coal taken from this with tongs.
Jesus taught: leave your gift in front of this, and first go make peace with your brother.
In Athens, Paul found one of these with the inscription TO AN UNKNOWN GOD.
Noah was 600 years old when this came upon the earth.
In Noah's time, it kept coming on the earth for forty days.
After beating the Philistines at Baal-perazim, David said the LORD burst out against his enemies like a bursting one.
In Jesus' story of the wise builder, this came against the house on the rock but could not shake it.
The prophet Nahum said God would make an end of Nineveh with an overwhelming one of these.
Jesus said that in the days before this, people were eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage.
After this event, the man who built the ark went on living for another 350 years.
The LORD told him to leave his country, his kindred and his father's household for a land He would show him.
He looked up and saw three men standing nearby, then ran from his tent entrance to meet them and bowed low.
Pleading with the LORD over Sodom, he asked again and again until God agreed to spare it for ten righteous people.
The LORD took him outside and told him to count the stars, saying his offspring would be like them.
He was a hundred years old when his long-awaited son was finally born to him.
Melchizedek, king of Salem, met him returning from the slaughter of the kings and blessed him.
In a story Jesus told, a rich man in Hades looked up and saw him far off, with Lazarus by his side.
The angel of the LORD said this unborn boy would be a wild donkey of a man, his hand against everyone.
God promised Abraham that this son would become the father of twelve rulers and a great nation.
He was thirteen years old when he was circumcised along with his father Abraham's household.
Sarah saw her husband Abraham's son by another woman mocking her own son.
Esau went to this son of Abraham and married his daughter Mahalath, the sister of Nebaioth.
He and his half brother Isaac buried their father Abraham in the cave of Machpelah.
When Hagar ran from Sarai, an angel told her to name her unborn son because the LORD heard her cry.
God came down on this mountain in fire, and it smoked like a furnace and shook violently.
Here the LORD gave Moses two stone tablets written by the finger of God.
Moses came down this mountain with his face shining from talking with the LORD, unaware of it.
Moses went into the cloud on this mountain and stayed there forty days and forty nights.
Stephen said an angel appeared to Moses in a burning bush in the desert near this mountain.
When Moses was slow to come down from this mountain, the Israelites asked Aaron to make them gods.
God told Moses to set a boundary around this mountain, warning that anyone who touched it would die.
Priests carrying the ark of the covenant stood in its middle while all Israel crossed over on dry ground.
Under Joshua, the Israelites took twelve stones from its middle, one for each tribe, and carried them to camp.
Naaman dipped himself in it seven times, as the man of God said, and his flesh was restored.
Jesus came from Nazareth in Galilee and was baptized by John in it.
Gideon and his three hundred men came to it and crossed it, exhausted yet still in pursuit.
God told Moses to look out over the land from the top of Pisgah, because he would not cross it.
At its fords, the Gileadites killed any Ephraimite who said Sibboleth instead of Shibboleth.
At the place God had designated, his father bound him and laid him on the altar atop the wood.
He prayed to the LORD for his wife because she was barren, and the LORD heard him and she conceived.
Abraham held a great feast on the day this child was weaned.
Meditating in a field one evening, he looked up and saw camels bringing his future bride.
Old and unable to see, he touched his son's hairy hands and said the voice did not match them.
After the herdsmen of Gerar quarreled over his wells, he dug another and named it Rehoboth.
At Gerar, the king of the Philistines looked down from a window and saw him caressing his wife.
Tending flocks for his father-in-law, he peeled fresh poplar, almond, and plane branches to expose the white wood.
Going on ahead of his family to meet Esau, he bowed to the ground seven times as he approached.
When he saw Rachel at a well, he rolled the stone from its mouth and watered his uncle Laban's sheep.
Traveling from Beersheba toward Haran, he dreamed of a ladder to heaven with God's angels going up and down.
The morning after his wedding, he found the wrong bride beside him and accused his father-in-law of deceiving him.
Wrestling a man until daybreak, he refused to let go unless the man blessed him.
Brought by Joseph before Pharaoh in Egypt, he said his travels had lasted 130 years.
In Solomon's song, the beloved is told her eyes are like doves behind this.
Tamar took off her widow's clothes and covered her face with this so Judah would not know her.
Moses put this back over his radiant face until he went in again to speak with the LORD.
God told Moses to hang this in the tabernacle, with the ark behind it, separating the Holy Place from the Most Holy Place.
At the moment Jesus yielded up His spirit, this in the temple was torn in two from top to bottom.
Paul wrote that this lies over hearts when Moses is read, but it is taken away when anyone turns to the Lord.
Whenever Israel's camp set out in the wilderness, Aaron and his sons took this down and covered the ark with it.
At a well near Haran, Jacob rolled the stone away and watered the sheep this shepherdess brought.
Jacob served Laban seven years for her, and it seemed but a few days because of his love.
After Jacob's wedding feast, Laban gave him her older sister Leah instead, and Jacob found out in the morning.
After years without children, Jacob's wife named her first son Joseph and asked the LORD for another son.
She let her sister Leah have Jacob for a night in exchange for some of Leah's son's mandrakes.
With her last breath, she named her newborn son Ben-oni, but Jacob called the boy Benjamin.
After Herod killed the boys of Bethlehem, Matthew recalled a voice in Ramah: she weeps for her children.
In Egypt, after Joseph made himself known, he threw his arms around this brother and they both wept.
During the famine, Jacob would not send this son to Egypt with his brothers, fearing harm.
At Joseph's meal in Egypt, this brother's portion was five times larger than anyone else's.
Joseph's steward searched the brothers' sacks and found the silver cup in this youngest brother's sack.
In Jacob's last blessings to his sons, this son is called a ravenous wolf that devours prey.
Saul told Samuel he came from this tribe, the smallest tribe of Israel.
Paul wrote that he was circumcised on the eighth day and belonged to this tribe of Israel.
In John's vision, an elder told him not to weep, for the Lion of this tribe had triumphed to open the scroll.
When his brothers planned to kill Joseph, this brother asked what profit they would gain from covering up his blood.
Told that his daughter-in-law Tamar was pregnant, this son of Jacob ordered her brought out and burned to death.
After Saul died, the men of this tribe came to Hebron and anointed David king over their house.
When the LORD in His anger removed Israel from His presence, only this tribe remained.
Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah were young men from this land, chosen to serve the king of Babylon.
Jacob said the scepter would not depart from this son, nor the staff from between his feet.
Lot looked out and saw the Jordan plain was well watered, like the garden of the LORD and like this land.
During the great famine, ten of Joseph's brothers traveled down to this land to buy grain.
In Solomon's day, a chariot could be imported from this land for six hundred shekels of silver.
When Solomon sought to kill Jeroboam, he fled here and stayed until Solomon's death.
Mocking King Hezekiah, the Assyrian envoy called this land a splintered reed that pierces the hand leaning on it.
Complaining in the wilderness, Israel remembered the fish, cucumbers, melons and leeks they ate freely here.
While Ishmael lived in the Wilderness of Paran, his mother got him a wife from this land.
Abraham weighed out four hundred of these in silver to Ephron the Hittite to buy a burial place for Sarah.
Elisha foretold that at Samaria's gate, a seah of fine flour would sell for just one of these.
While hunting lost donkeys, Saul's servant offered a quarter of one in silver to pay the man of God.
The Philistine giant who taunted Israel's army wore bronze scale armor weighing five thousand of these.
Moses collected five of these for each firstborn Israelite beyond the number of the Levites, to redeem them.
In the law of vows given through Moses, a man aged twenty to sixty was valued at fifty of these in silver.
Amos condemned merchants who wanted to shrink the ephah, make this bigger, and cheat with dishonest scales.
The angel of the LORD appeared to him in a blazing fire within a bush, yet the bush was not consumed.
This leader of Israel died at a hundred and twenty, yet his eyes were not weak and his vitality had not diminished.
He stretched out his hand over the sea at daybreak, and the waters returned upon the fleeing Egyptians.
God told him to chisel out two new stone tablets to replace the first ones, which he had broken.
The Israelites saw that his face was radiant after speaking with the LORD, so he covered it with a veil.
During the battle with Amalek, Aaron and Hur held up his tired hands until the sun went down.
Pharaoh's daughter took this child as her own son and named him because she drew him out of the water.
As the people waited for Moses to come down the mountain, this leader told them to bring him their gold earrings.
In front of Pharaoh and his officials, he raised his staff and struck the Nile, and its water turned to blood.
When the LORD's anger burned against Moses, He named this brother who could speak well and was coming to meet him.
As Joshua fought the Amalekites, he and Hur held up Moses' tired hands until sunset.
His sons Nadab and Abihu put incense in their censers and offered unauthorized fire before the LORD.
On Mount Hor his priestly garments were put on his son Eleazar, and he died there.
When a plague broke out after Korah's rebellion, he ran among the people with incense and made atonement.
Leah named her third son this, hoping her husband Jacob would at last become attached to her.
With his brother Simeon, he took a sword into Shechem and killed its men to avenge their sister Dinah.
After the golden calf, Moses called for whoever was for the LORD, and this tribe gathered around him.
In Egypt, the parents of the baby Moses, hidden in a basket by the Nile, both came from this family line.

In the wilderness, the LORD set this tribe apart to carry the ark of the covenant and pronounce blessings.

Elisha told his servant Gehazi that this would cling to him and his descendants forever.
At the LORD's word, Moses put his hand inside his cloak and drew it out with this.

After God called them a stiff-necked people, the Israelites stripped off their jewelry from this mountain onward.

A psalm recalls that at this place the Israelites made a calf and worshiped a molten image.

Here the angel of the LORD appeared to Moses in a bush that blazed with fire but was not consumed.
When Solomon's priests set the ark in the temple, it held only the two stone tablets Moses placed in it here.
On the mountain, Isaac's father found one caught by its horns in a thicket and offered it instead of his son.

Moses was told to cover the tabernacle tent with its skins, dyed red.

After the priests circled Jericho the seventh time and blew their horns, he commanded the people to shout.

Abram moved his tent to live near the Oaks of Mamre in this town and built an altar there.
Abraham buried his wife Sarah in the cave of the field at Machpelah, near this town in Canaan.

Absalom asked King David to let him go to this town to fulfill a vow to the LORD.

This father had seven sons pass before Samuel, then said the youngest was still out tending the sheep.

Isaiah foretold a shoot springing up from this man's stump, and a Branch bearing fruit from his roots.

Deborah told him the LORD had gone before him, so he led his men down Mount Tabor against Sisera.

Deborah warned this commander the honor would not be his, because the LORD would hand Sisera to a woman.

In the song of Deborah and Barak, the stars fought against him from their courses.

When Pharaoh's army chased Israel into the sea, the LORD made the wheels of these wobble.

Moses fled from Pharaoh to this land and sat down beside a well.
Moses' father-in-law Jethro served as the priest of this land.

The men of Ephraim captured Oreb and Zeeb, two princes of this people, and brought their heads to Gideon.

Elders of this people went with Moab's elders to Balaam, carrying fees for divination and Balak's message.

The LORD told him to keep only the three hundred men who lapped the water and send the others home.

His father Gilead's other sons drove him out, saying he was the son of another woman.
After fleeing his brothers to the land of Tob, this man of Gilead gathered worthless men around him.
When the Ammonites made war on Israel, the elders of Gilead came asking this man to be their commander.

The men of Ephraim threatened to burn his house down with him inside for fighting the Ammonites without them.

At Samson's wedding feast, the Philistine men answered his riddle by asking what is stronger than this.
A man of God disobeyed the LORD, and one killed him on the road but left his donkey unharmed.
Young David told Saul he had killed these, along with bears, while guarding his father's sheep.
Peter warned that the devil prowls around like a roaring one, seeking someone to devour.
In John's vision, an elder said the one of the tribe of Judah, the Root of David, could open the scroll.
Daniel told King Darius that God sent His angel to shut the mouths of these, so they did not hurt him.
Isaiah foresaw a peaceful day when this fierce animal would eat straw like the ox.
During the long siege of Samaria, the head of one sold for eighty shekels of silver.
After Balaam beat his mount three times, the LORD opened its mouth and it spoke to him.
Near the Mount of Olives, Jesus sent two disciples to untie one tied with her colt and bring both.
Abraham saddled one early in the morning before setting out with Isaac and wood for a burnt offering.
Abigail came riding one into a mountain ravine and met David and his men coming down.
The law Moses gave said each firstborn one must be redeemed with a lamb, or its neck broken.
Heading back to Egypt from Midian, Moses put his wife and sons on one and took the staff of God.
Moses warned that if Israel disobeyed, these trees would fill their land, but the fruit would drop off unused.
When the trees sought a king in Jotham's story, this tree refused, unwilling to stop giving its oil.
In a vision, Zechariah saw two of these trees beside a solid gold lampstand, one on each side.
Paul told Gentile believers they were a wild shoot grafted into this tree to share its nourishing root.
On the night He was betrayed, Jesus went as usual to the mount named for these trees to pray.

He tied torches between the tails of three hundred foxes and burned the Philistines' standing grain.

During a seven-day feast, he bet thirty linen garments on a riddle about something sweet coming out of the strong.
Of her two widowed Moabite daughters-in-law, Orpah kissed her goodbye, but Ruth clung to her.

After her family moved to Moab during a famine, she lost her husband Elimelech and then both her sons.
On the road back to Judah, she urged her two Moabite daughters-in-law to return to their mothers' homes.
When Ruth came home from gleaning in Boaz's field, this woman told her that Boaz was one of their kinsman-redeemers.
She told Ruth to wash, put on perfume and her best clothes, and go to Boaz's threshing floor at night.
After Ruth and Boaz had a son, this grandmother placed the child on her lap and became his nurse.
Urged to leave her mother-in-law Naomi, she replied, "Your people will be my people, and your God will be my God."
Gleaning grain behind the harvesters near Bethlehem, she happened to come to the part of the field owned by Boaz.

Matthew's list of Jesus' ancestors names her as the mother of Obed, the father of Jesse.

When Jesus fed five thousand, a boy offered five loaves made from it, along with two small fish.

Absalom had his servants set fire to Joab's field of this grain so Joab would come see him.

Naomi came back to Bethlehem from this land with her daughter-in-law Ruth as the barley harvest began.
Lot's older daughter gave her son this name, and he became the father of a whole people.
Balak son of Zippor, king of this land, sent for Balaam son of Beor to curse Israel.
The LORD buried Moses in a valley in this land, and no one knows where his grave is.
Ehud, a left-handed Benjamite, was sent with tribute to Eglon, the king of this land.
While hiding from danger, David asked this land's king to let his father and mother stay with him.

At Bethel, Jacob set up the stone he had slept on as one and poured oil on top.
